uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: component mount, before getService(id) has resolved or rejected — service === null && error === false — renders three pulsing skeleton rows
uiStatesHandled.reachable: yes — always transiently entered, getMockService has a 250ms delay

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: getService(id) resolves to null (no MOCK_SERVICES entry matches id) or the promise rejects — error === true — renders <ErrorState title="Service not found" .../>
uiStatesHandled.reachable: yes — reachable today by navigating to /services/<id> for any id not in MOCK_SERVICES and not matched by a sibling static route (cac/nepc/mentors/applications); getMockService(id) returns null for unmatched ids

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: getService(id) resolves to a PartnerService and notified === false (initial state) — renders icon/name/tagline/blurb, 'Pro members first' card, and a 'Notify me when it launches' button
uiStatesHandled.reachable: yes. Note: this layout is rendered unconditionally regardless of the fetched service.status value — the component never branches on status, so if this route were ever reached for a 'live' service it would still show the coming-soon copy and CTA. In practice this is masked because Next.js route precedence resolves /services/cac, /services/nepc and /services/mentors to their own static page.tsx files (outside this screen's scope) before falling through to [id]/page.tsx, so only the four 'coming' services (health-insurance, pension, banking, grants-funding) are ever actually served by this component today.

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: user clicks 'Notify me when it launches' → notify() calls notifyComingSoon(id) and awaits it → notified === true — renders a green check banner 'You're on the list — we'll tell you the moment it launches.'
uiStatesHandled.reachable: yes — notifyMockComingSoon() always resolves true after a 400ms delay, so this state is reachable on every click under current mocks. No error/failure UI exists for a rejected notifyComingSoon call — the click handler has no try/catch.
